prize_parts.citation: for empirical analyses of how import competition and technological change reshape labour demand, local labour markets and wage inequality

statement.case_for: My configuration has changed. In round 1 I ranked B029 first and B022 as my first alternative. I now put B022 first. The change comes from three arguments, not from the number of colleagues who prefer it. First, the exchange sharpened what exactly each prize would name. The China-shock papers are jointly Autor, Dorn and Hanson, and the discovery is that adjustment to trade and technology shocks is slow, costly and concentrated in particular places. That finding is attributable to a three-person set and is stated in one sentence. Second, the empirical record is long and open to scrutiny. The designs are transparent, and the work has been re-analysed, extended to other countries and criticised for roughly a decade. The debate concerns the size and persistence of the effects, not whether adjustment costs exist. As someone who works in the design-based tradition, I think a finding that has survived hostile re-examination is a good basis for a prize. Third, my own B029 case rests on an attribution problem I could not resolve in discussion. I could not settle Bresnahan's claim against Berry or Levinsohn, and nobody with deep field expertise made a case that would settle it. I still think the BLP and Ericson-Pakes work is prize-level, so B029 stays an alternative. I propose the citation rest on the empirical evidence, with no claim to the task-model theory, so that it names what can be attributed to the three.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is that the quantitative claims remain contested: the magnitude and persistence of the China-shock effects, and the sensitivity of shift-share designs to identification critiques. The citation therefore has to be worded with care, and the Scientific Background should address the re-analyses directly. Credit for the task framework extends beyond the credited set (Acemoglu, Levy, Murnane), and the 2024 prize touches nearby themes, so a citation that reached into task-model theory would overstate what these three did. There is also a fair objection that this is mainly a research-design and measurement prize and less a conceptual advance than B012. I should add that I work in design-based empirical labour economics and have an obvious affinity for this kind of evidence. That affinity is not evidence of merit, and I have tried to guard against it by asking what is attributable and confirmed, not what resembles my own work. If the Committee judges the identification critiques to be more damaging than I do, B012 or B029 would be the natural fallbacks.

responses.point: Enflo asked me how I separate the methods contribution of B029 from the economic findings it enabled, and said she would reconsider B029 if the argument were strong. She ranks B022 first on the basis of causal identification, transparent designs and the first-order importance of the question.
responses.response: I tried to answer her question for myself and it moved me. The BLP estimator and the Ericson-Pakes framework are enabling tools, and the findings they produced are spread over many applications by many authors: mergers, trade, health, energy. A citation can name market power and welfare, but the discovery being credited is still mainly the tool. By contrast, the China-shock papers contain the finding itself, together with the design that identifies it, and they are a single body of work. That does not make B029 inferior, but it makes the citation harder to write without it reading as a methods prize so soon after 2021. I therefore take her criterion seriously and now apply it to my own first choice, which is why I changed.

responses.point: Krusell also ranks B029 first. He argues that the BLP and Ericson-Pakes methods allow counterfactuals on prices, mergers and welfare that design-based methods generally cannot provide, and that the citation should name market power and competition as the subject. He keeps the BLP trio with moderate confidence on Bresnahan.
responses.response: His counterfactual argument is the strongest reason B029 is prize-level, and I accept it. Structural estimation answers questions that quasi-experiments cannot, and that complementarity is real. I do not move because I doubt it. I move because, on the common criteria, I cannot separate the discovery from the estimator in the citation, and the seven-name ballot leaves Bresnahan unresolved, which we have both said openly. Only a few members ranked B029 in the opening round, and I do not treat that as a merit judgement either way. But it means the Committee has tested the case less. I would keep B029 as the lead alternative and would back it if members with field expertise settle the Bresnahan question.

responses.point: Hassler, who moved from B021 to B012, ranks B012 first. He argues that firm heterogeneity has the broader and better-confirmed reach, with more than two decades of confirmation across theory, microdata and policy evaluation. He also notes that B029 would be read mainly as a methods prize and that its seven-name ballot invites a dispute over Bresnahan.
responses.response: I agree with him on B029, and that is part of why I moved. On B012 versus B022, I think the question is what each discovery explains. Melitz and Helpman changed how economists understand selection and reallocation in trade, and that is a mature, well-confirmed advance. B022 provides credibly identified evidence on who bears the adjustment costs, which trade theory does not address. I cannot say one is more important, and I treat them as different kinds of contributions. I rank B022 higher mainly because the attribution is cleaner within the work that is credited and because the evidence has been tested by sustained critique. His point about welfare results depending on functional form, such as the Pareto assumption, is fair and is a reason B012 is not clearly the safer choice. B012 remains my second alternative.

responses.point: Strömberg prefers B012 over B022 on maturity and scope. He argues that the persistence and magnitude of the China-shock effects are still being revised, while the core insight of the heterogeneous-firm framework has not been overturned. He keeps B022 as an alternative and says he would not oppose it.
responses.response: I accept that the magnitudes are being revised, and I do not want to understate it. I would distinguish the headline estimates from the finding the citation would name. Several re-analyses have adjusted the size and duration of the effects, but the finding that adjustment is slow and costly in exposed local labour markets has held across settings, as far as I can tell from the openings. If the Committee prefers a prize whose core has not been revised at all, B012 is the more conservative choice, and I would not call that choice wrong. I would only say that revision under scrutiny is evidence the work has been taken seriously, not that it is immature.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson ranks B022 first and uses the wording 'empirical and conceptual analyses'. In her round-1 reply to me she said the citation should be built around what is clearly attributable, the empirical analysis of technology and import competition, and that the disputes concern magnitude and persistence, not direction.
responses.response: I agree with her reply to me, and it is the reasoning I now adopt. On the chair's wording question, I would drop 'conceptual' from the citation. The conceptual task framework has originators outside the credited set, so claiming it invites the attribution problem the three-name cap cannot solve. I would use 'empirical analyses' and tie the wording to labour demand and local labour markets. I would also ask that the Scientific Background handle the persistence re-analyses directly. This makes the citation narrower than some members might like, but it matches what Autor, Dorn and Hanson can be credited with.

uncertainties: How far the re-analyses of China-shock persistence and magnitude, and the critiques of shift-share designs, should qualify the award. I cannot settle this from the supplied evidence.
Whether a citation can stay on the empirical evidence without understating the task framework's other originators (Acemoglu, Levy, Murnane), and how the 2024 prize's thematic proximity should weigh.

Whether B022 versus B012 can be ranked on common criteria at all, since they cover different ground. My preference rests on attribution clarity and the record of scrutiny, and a reasonable member could weigh originality and breadth of confirmation more heavily.
Whether Bresnahan's claim on B029 would outweigh Levinsohn or Berry, and whether B029 would be read as a methods prize after 2021. I have not resolved this and still regard B029 as prize-level.
My account of credit shares and the replication record rests on general knowledge and the supplied round-1 files. I have not independently verified it.
statement.conflict_note: No tie to Autor, Dorn or Hanson, or to the alternatives' credited names (Pakes, Berry, Levinsohn, Melitz, Helpman), is apparent from the supplied profile. I disclose that my own class-size paper (with Öckert and Oosterbeek) is cited in the 2021 Scientific Background, that I chaired the Committee in 2019-21 and gave the 2021 presentation speech, and that my work is in the design-based empirical labour tradition closest to B022. That affinity may shape my judgement and is expertise, not merit. My Stockholm University overlap with Hassler and Krusell is institutional, not co-authorship. I have changed my preferred ballot since round 1, and the profile does not record any new connection. These are disclosed, not adjudicated.
